The right platform pairs medical record acquisition with AI-powered analysis that flags potential breach-of-care issues, surfaces missing documentation, and pulls out future medical expense information for attorney review, with humans verifying the insights. This guide covers the top ChartSquad alternatives and why[Codes Health](https://www.getcodeshealth.com/) stands out for firms that want managed retrieval and legal-focused AI analysis in one workflow, with records in a couple of weeks, not months.

-


Codes Health stands out as a leading ChartSquad alternative, combining managed medical record retrieval with AI-generated insights verified by humans, missing record detection, and flat fee pricing


-


ChartSquad uses a patient-controlled PHR workflow that involves patient setup and permissions, while the company handles provider follow-up; firm-managed services handle requests on the firm's side instead


-

-

## **Why Law Firms Seek ChartSquad Alternatives**


ChartSquad operates a patient-controlled Personal Health Record platform that uses HIPAA right-of-access rules to obtain records through patient-directed requests. ChartSquad advertises an average provider fee of $6.50 for its patient-access model; actual charges and applicable fee rules depend on the request. The workflow involves patient setup and permissions, while ChartSquad handles provider communications and follow-up. ChartSquad also advertises AI medical record summaries, case management connectivity, a custom API, and chronologies and demand packages delivered through partners.


**Common reasons firms evaluate alternatives:**


-


Preference for firm-managed workflows that keep patient setup steps off the client's plate


-


Interest in legal-specific AI analysis built into the retrieval service itself


-


Demand for potential breach-of-care flags in medical malpractice cases


-


Missing record detection to check completeness before trial preparation


-


Human verification of AI outputs for high-stakes litigation


-


Integration with existing case management systems


Medical record retrieval has moved beyond simple document collection. Plaintiff firms now look for platforms that turn raw medical data into usable case intelligence while checking completeness to avoid trial surprises.


## **1. Codes Health**


[Codes Health](https://www.getcodeshealth.com/) is a comprehensive ChartSquad alternative for plaintiff law firms, combining multi-channel medical record retrieval with purpose-built AI analysis and human verification. Codes Health manages retrieval and checks for potential gaps, with advertised turnaround of a couple of weeks. Timing and any required client input depend on the request.

-

Pre-submission checking matters more than it might seem. Incomplete authorizations are a leading preventable cause of denied requests. Missing patient signatures, unclear expiration dates, or unchecked boxes for sensitive records can force a resubmission and put a request back at the start of the provider's response window. Under the[30-day federal standard](https://www.hhs.gov/hipaa/for-professionals/faq/how-timely-must-a-covered-entity-be/index.html) for HIPAA access requests, providers generally have 30 calendar days to act, and state timelines vary. Codes Health's AI review catches these errors before submission, automatically flagging misspellings, missing dates of service, and signature issues that would otherwise cause provider rejections.


Through the[Filevine partnership](https://www.prnewswire.com/news-releases/filevine-partners-with-codes-health-to-bring-ai-native-medical-record-retrieval-to-legal-teams-302823827.html) announced on July 13, 2026, Filevine users can submit requests, track progress, communicate with the Codes Health team, and receive completed records without leaving their case file.

### **Market Position**

### **Pricing**

## **Ensuring Data Completeness in Medical Record Retrieval**


Completeness is one of the clearest differences between retrieval platforms. Incomplete records create real litigation risk, from weakened damages arguments to surprise evidence at trial.


Platforms differ in three separate capabilities, and each is worth comparing on its own:


-


**Flagging potential gaps** : Several analysis tools, including Legalyze and EvenUp, advertise gap detection within supplied records


-


**Finding additional providers** : Some services, including Codes Health and LlamaLab, describe ways to surface providers the client didn't list


-


**Retrieving missing documents** : Managed retrieval services, such as Codes Health, ChartRequest, and RRS, describe follow-up on incomplete records


Codes Health combines all three in one workflow. AI flags potential gaps based on treatment patterns and provider history, and the team works with facilities to resolve identified gaps before delivery.


## **Integration Capabilities for Law Firms**


Case management works best when data flows cleanly between retrieval platforms and legal systems. Integration depth varies across alternatives.


**Integration considerations:**


-


**Case management synchronization** : Cutting manual data transfer between retrieval vendors and platforms like Filevine, Clio, or Litify


-


**Document delivery workflows** : Receiving completed records directly into case files instead of separate portals


-


**Status visibility** : Tracking retrieval progress without leaving the case management environment


-


**Communication centralization** : Managing vendor correspondence within case records


Codes Health's Filevine partnership lets firms initiate requests, track progress, communicate with the retrieval team, and receive completed records without leaving their case management workspace. For high-volume customers, Codes Health builds custom integrations with CRM platforms and other medical software to match existing workflows.


## **Why General AI Tools Fall Short**


General AI platforms like ChatGPT are not designed for litigation-grade medical record review. AI-generated medical record analysis can contain errors or omissions, so attorneys should verify material findings against source records and assess each tool's suitability and confidentiality safeguards, consistent with[ABA ethics guidance](https://www.americanbar.org/news/abanews/aba-news-archives/2024/07/aba-issues-first-ethics-guidance-ai-tools/) on AI use. Codes Health's purpose-built platform is designed to analyze medical records with high precision for plaintiff firms, flagging potential standard-of-care departures, missed diagnoses, and treatment delays, with human verification as an added quality-control step.

## **The Bottom Line**


Most record problems in plaintiff cases are preventable: authorizations rejected over a missing signature, record sets that come back without certain providers or date ranges, and gaps that only show up when trial prep is already underway. Fast turnaround doesn't solve those on its own, and a quick partial delivery can push the follow-up work back onto your team and your clients.


What prevents those failures is checking requests before submission, following up until providers respond, and confirming completeness before the file closes.
